analysis: This PR adds only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/flint-decode-fusions.md, head lines 1-3) and a new paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head hunk at ~2513-2520). Neither file changes code, configuration, endpoints, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache behavior. The prose describes SDK-level decode kernel fusions: fused q/k/v and gate/up projections, routed gate/up banks fused at load, compiled router steps, and one MoE combine/residual kernel. It claims byte-identical outputs and about 40% fewer GPU dispatches, and says the checkpoint is still validated in split form. It describes no change to TB-007 data handling, such as encryption, plaintext exposure, the prefix cache in T-041, or residual GPU data in T-028. It adds no new input surface, and the described fusions are internal compute-graph optimizations inside the same process memory. The actual SDK pin and kernel changes are not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that the fused kernels introduce no output divergence, since T-007 and T-056 cover correctness overclaims. It should also check that fused-weight loading keeps the split-form checkpoint and weight-hash validation (T-012, T-027) intact. The 'byte-identical' claim is an unverified performance and correctness assertion, not a security regression. The supplied base_text excerpt does not reach the changed hunk, so I relied on the patch for that unit. The documentation hunk contains no secrets and no instruction-like content.
